sentences.sentence: The NHS links intense pain around the time of a period, sometimes with pain during or after sex and when pooing, with endometriosis.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved text links intense pain around the time of a period (with possible pain during/after sex and when pooing) to endometriosis. Plain 'period pain' as a listed cause, and 'lower tummy in women', were not seen.

sentences.sentence: The NHS stomach ache page links pain in the lower right side of the tummy with appendicitis.

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales links severe pain that lasts for hours in the upper centre of the tummy, or just under the ribs on the right, with gallstones.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS 111 Wales lists gallstones for severe pain lasting hours in the upper centre of the tummy or under the right ribs. nhs.uk gallstones says pain usually lasts 1 to 5 hours; 8 hours is a GP-contact threshold, not a duration of the pain. Attribution to the NHS stomach ache page not confirmed.

sentences.sentence: It links ongoing cramps, bloating, diarrhoea and constipation with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform describes appendicitis as painful swelling of the appendix, and says the pain and cramping of IBS may be relieved by going to the toilet.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS inform: appendicitis is painful swelling of the appendix (supported). For IBS it says pain and cramping 'may be relieved by moving your bowels'; 'often' overstates.

sentences.sentence: Stomach ulcer pain is usually in the upper tummy, may feel burning and is often worse at night.

sentences.sentence: Gastritis can cause pain, indigestion and feeling sick.

sentences.sentence: Acute pancreatitis causes severe pain around the top of the tummy that develops suddenly, and gallstones and alcohol are its most common causes.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS: severe dull pain around the top of the stomach that develops suddenly (upper abdomen), not the centre generally; gallstones about half and alcohol about a quarter of cases.

sentences.sentence: Appendicitis is when the appendix becomes inflamed; it usually causes pain in the lower right side of the tummy and is sometimes accompanied by nausea and loss of appetite.

sentences.sentence: Many people with gallstones have no symptoms, but a stone can cause pain, jaundice or pancreatitis.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: The Chesterfield (cht.nhs.uk) page did not come back. NHS gallstones results say most people with gallstones never get symptoms, and a stone can cause pain, jaundice (blocked bile duct) or pancreatitis (blocked pancreatic duct).

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says diverticulitis, the inflamed form of diverticular disease, tends to cause more severe tummy pain, especially on the left side, and a fever.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved: lower left-sided pain; NHS inform says diverticulitis is more serious, with more severe pain especially on the left, fever of 38C or above, diarrhoea. Worse after eating / eases after wind or stool and the symptom list were not seen; nhs.uk page itself did not return.

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises urgent help from a GP or NHS 111 for blood or mucus in the stool, pain that gets worse or does not go away, or a high temperature or shivers.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Only NHS 111 Wales text retrieved: urgent GP or 111 for blood or mucus in stool, pain that worsens or will not go away, high temperature or shivers, persistent vomiting. The 999/A&E list in the sentence was not confirmed; snippets cut off before it. Route to care and publisher not matched.
